items.title: Compact shell mounts the mini-player twice
items.reproduction: app/src/main/java/com/tunenagi/player/ui/shell/TunenagiShell.kt passed MiniPlayerHost both to Scaffold(bottomBar=...) and to the content Column. In ShellLayout.Compact with MiniPlayerState.Track both were composed: the bottom bar reserved the bar's height twice and the semantics tree held two nodes with TestTag 'mini-player' (measured: node #172 at t=218..304px and node #123 at t=304..390px). Found by TunenagiShellTest on the JVM (Robolectric): 'Failed to perform checkIsDisplayed check: Expected at most 1 node but found 2 nodes that satisfy (TestTag = mini-player)'. SPEC/UX_DESIGN.md requires the mini-player to sit above the navigation bar, i.e. exactly once.
items.resolution: Fixed in TunenagiShell.kt: the layout now mounts exactly one MiniPlayerHost per layout (compact: inside the bottom-bar Column above the navigation bar; wide: closing the content column), with the decision hoisted into miniPlayerVisible/layout so the two call sites cannot disagree again. Retest: :app:testDebugUnitTest --rerun-tasks rebuilt and ran the shell suite on the JVM, exit 0, 8 tests / 0 failures, including two new regression tests asserting exactly one 'mini-player' and one navigation container node in each layout.

items.title: Source loss is not covered by a deletes-a-source test
items.reproduction: SPEC/DATA_MODEL.md: 'source can disappear without deleting Track/PlaylistEntry'. The phase-01 trap list names 'accidental deletion after source loss'. Phase 01 asserts the opposite direction (DatabaseConstraintTest.deletingATrackCascadesItsDependentsAndKeepsTheAlbum) and asserts that an unavailable source stays in the library (SourceMatchRepositoryTest.anAvailabilityChangeOnTheLockedSourceDoesNotUnlockIt, MigrationTest seeds a Restricted source), but no test deletes a track_sources row and checks that the track, its credit and its playlist entry survive. Found by the phase-01 audit while checking each named trap.
items.resolution: Added DatabaseConstraintTest.deletingASourceLeavesTheTrackCreditsAndPlaylistsIntact: it removes the track_sources row outright and asserts the track, its credit row, its playlist entry and its favourite all survive, and that the track's source count drops to zero. Retest: the :core::database suite ran green (exit 0) with the new test included.

items.title: A disconnect while the controller was still binding left the app permanently Closed
items.reproduction: PlaybackConnection.disconnect() released through controller?.let { ... }, so while a MediaController was still binding (controller == null, controllerFuture != null) it released nothing: controllerFuture survived, and every later connect() returned early on if (controllerFuture != null). The connection then stayed Closed for the rest of the process with the service binding still held, and only an app restart could recover. onError() had the same shape: it reported Failed and left an attached controller in place. Found while writing the teardown test; proved by mutation - reverting disconnect() to the guarded form makes NowPlayingTest.disconnectingWhileConnectingLetsTheNextConnectTryAgain fail with expected:<Connecting> but was:<Closed> (STATE/evidence/TUN-0201/20261015T194929Z-old-disconnect-mutation-fails.json, exit 1).
items.resolution: All three teardown paths (explicit disconnect, service disconnect, session error) now release through one private controllerRelease() that clears both the attached controller and the pending future, and is idempotent. Retest: :app:testDebugUnitTest --tests NowPlayingTest --rerun-tasks -> exit 0, 6 tests / 0 failures, including the new regression test that fails against the old code. Full gate re-run afterwards: python SCRIPTS/verify.py -> exit 0, 9/9 steps.
